user.title: Bedtime Bridge
user.description: Choose what Snooze and Stop on your iPhone do in Home Assistant, and which entities the app should read when it plans your alarms.

data.home_only: Only run routines when you're home
data.bedtime_helper: Turn on to start the bedtime routine
data.wake_action: When you snooze or stop an alarm
data.shift_types: Shift types (comma separated, as they appear in calendar titles)
data.replan_alert: Tell me when my plan goes out of date
data.rearm_minutes: Re-arm after back in bed for

data_description.wake_action: Helpers: turn on the entities below, for blueprints that watch them (Wake Snooze Fade, Wake Sequence). Events: fire a bedtime_bridge event for automations and blueprints to trigger on. Both: do both.
data_description.shift_types: Each one gets a lead-time setting, and its name is sent as the alarm cause.
data_description.home_only: Snooze, stop and Start Bedtime Routine skip the helpers and wake events while you're away. If your location is unknown, you count as home.
data_description.bedtime_helper: Turned on by the app's Start Bedtime Routine action (e.g. input_boolean.bedtime_routine).
data_description.safety_net_causes: Publishes safety-net times after the last alarm for these alarm causes, for a Wake Deadline Backstop instance: early at the last alarm, deadline (out of bed) one margin later, late (left the room) two margins later. Shift mornings already have your own rung sensors, so the default is calendar only.
data_description.notify_service: e.g. notify.mobile_app_mikes_iphone. Used for the re-plan notification and phone commands.
data_description.replan_alert: If the shift override or your next shift changes after you planned (and before you wake), send a notification with a Re-plan button.
data_description.bed_sensor: With the helper below, tells the app whether you're really up when you stop an alarm, so it keeps the later alarms if you're still in bed. Empty only counts after a minute (the sensor drops out briefly).
data_description.exit_latch: e.g. input_boolean.bedroom_exited_today, set by Bedroom Exit Latch when you open the bedroom door.
data_description.phone_commands: Pushes RUN_DISARM, RUN_ARM_STAY and RUN_GOOD_MORNING to the notify action above, for Shortcuts "When I receive a notification" automations on the phone: disarm for a temporary alarm, re-arm once you're back in bed, and your morning shortcut when you stop a regular alarm (app alarms don't trigger Clock automations).
data_description.rearm_minutes: After a temporary alarm that disarmed the house, the bed sensor must read occupied this long without a break before RUN_ARM_STAY is sent. Not back in bed before your regular alarms (or within 6 hours): it doesn't re-arm.
data_description.sleep_in_helper: Turned on when your first alarm is after the curtains open and off when it's before, each time the phone plans, and on when you skip a morning to sleep in. Only while you're home. Temporary alarms never touch it.
data_description.curtain_offset_minutes: Match your curtain automation's open time (sunrise plus this).
data_description.home_check_entities: Doors, locks and the garage the app's Away Bedtime Summary checks when you go to bed away from home. Anything open, unlocked or not responding is read out; otherwise it says everything at home is good.

pair.title: Pair your iPhone
pair.description:
To pair your iPhone, open this step in the Home Assistant app on the iPhone and tap:

**[Pair Bedtime Bridge]({pair_link})**

That saves both addresses in the app. If the link doesn't open, copy it into the app's address field (Settings › Home Assistant):

`{pair_link}`

Or paste the addresses one by one:

- **Anywhere** (Nabu Casa): `{remote_url}`
- **At home only**: `{local_url}`

The app uses the first and falls back to the second if your internet is down at home. Keep them private: anyone with them can send alarm updates.

You can see this again under the integration's Configure.

abort.already_configured: Bedtime Bridge is already set up.
